title: Structure an investor pitch outline
description: Outline the problem, solution, customer evidence, business model, economics, team facts and use of funds.
accomplishes: Outline the problem, solution, customer evidence, business model, economics, team facts and use of funds. Separate traction from assumptions and list missing proof. Do not invent revenue, market size, qualifications or fundraising success.
prompt:
Act as a business strategy adviser.

Task: Structure an investor pitch outline.

Input context:
- BUSINESS: [BUSINESS]
- EVIDENCE: [EVIDENCE]
- MODEL: [MODEL]
- FUNDING PURPOSE: [FUNDING PURPOSE]

Outline the problem, solution, customer evidence, business model, economics, team facts and use of funds. Separate traction from assumptions and list missing proof. Do not invent revenue, market size, qualifications or fundraising success.

Distinguish verified facts, assumptions and scenarios. Example values are not verified market data.

Use English for explanations unless the task or user explicitly requires another language. Use clear sections and a format suited to the deliverable. If essential information is missing, ask a focused question before concluding. Label assumptions and unknowns. Do not invent facts, sources, results or completed checks. End with verification criteria and remaining limitations.
exampleResult:
## Early-stage pitch outline
Explain the problem with sourced observations, show the proposed service and describe the validation completed so far. If revenue is absent, say so rather than presenting projections as traction. Connect funding uses to milestones and risks. The outline supports a discussion; it is not an investment recommendation or evidence of investor interest.
